A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Snellcaster research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A-C. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of all equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments on 300 scene-object combinations, captured-scene examples, and component ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative experiments in Tables 1-4, captured-scene examples in Figure 5, and supplementary qualitative and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix B replaces the reported auxiliary LLM for prompt decomposition from ChatGPT to Gemma. This is a limited model-component substitution; the decomposition procedure, ray tracing, cross-view synchronization, generation backbone, and relighting procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same indoor/outdoor prompt coverage, six object geometries, 300 scene-object combinations, and captured-scene evaluations. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain FLUX Inpaint, FLUX-dev, FLUX.2-dev, Qwen-Image, and Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large. Qualitative comparator membership is also unchanged. ChatGPT and Gemma serve as auxiliary tools, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B revises the stated prompt-preprocessing model from ChatGPT to Gemma. This changes a reported preprocessing setting, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Sample counts, metrics, generation resolutions, denoising settings, and evaluation controls remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reflection, panorama, relighting, detail-preserving averaging, Laplacian warping, and time-travel ablations are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same refractive-index sweep and time-travel sensitivity analysis, with no analysis of the LLM substitution.

E5.justification: Random-seed reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1-4 and all qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Snellcaster's CLIP 32.85, ImageReward -0.32, PSNR 16.51, and LPIPS 0.24. No new outcome is reported for the auxiliary-model substitution.

T1.justification: The optical assumptions, mathematical definitions, and Equations 1-14 are unchanged, as is Appendix A's supporting account. Citation renumbering does not alter the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free generation of transparent objects and synchronization for physically consistent refractions, reflections, and unseen regions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ablations, relighting-versus-pixel-metric tradeoff, panorama completion, and time-travel smoothing remain unchanged. The same applicability restrictions and cautions about Blender-based reference metrics are retained.

D1.justification: The auxiliary-model specification changes: v2 names ChatGPT and cites version 5.1, whereas v3 names Gemma and cites its model-family paper without specifying a checkpoint or size. Prompts, other implementation details, hardware, and runtime reporting remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The OpenAI ChatGPT reference in v2 is removed and the Gemma Team's 2024 model paper is added in v3. Other affected references are merely renumbered; the related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the auxiliary-model name in Appendix B, associated citation numbering, the bibliography entry, and the arXiv version/date stamp. There is no substantive paragraph rewriting or section reorganization.

P2.justification: The replacement bibliography entry causes a small reflow on PDF page 10, with the Gemma reference spanning the two columns. All thirteen figures and four tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The revision substitutes an auxiliary LLM and updates its reference, while retaining the same supplied prompts, core generation procedure, results, analyses, and conclusions. Gemma's configuration is less specifically identified, but this limited documentation difference does not materially alter the paper's overall evidential support or explanatory quality.
